thruster.reason: owner constraint: thrusters sit at the platform's south/bottom edge, which is where a real platform mounts them

asteroid-collector.reason: owner constraint: collectors sit at an edge with their arms facing outward, off the platform

entity-ghost.reason: a ghost of WHAT is a coverage dimension: cryogenic-plant is the richest platform-legal crafting machine measured at this pin (6 fluidboxes, 8 module slots, against chemical-plant's 4 and 3), and it is the same prototype the derivation picked to represent assembling-machine, so the ghost mirrors the fixture's richest crafter

tile-ghost.reason: a ghost of WHAT is a coverage dimension: foundation is the only tile a platform builds out of, so it is the sole tile ghost a real platform can hold

item-request-proxy.reason: a proxy is created onto an existing entity, so it is placed after every other cell and shares its target's cell; the request shape is the one tests/integration/gateway-park-proxies proves the engine accepts

character-corpse.reason: core/deserializer.lua passes inventory_size when it restores a character-corpse, so the cell must carry a non-default inventory; the stock is load-bearing — measured 2026-08-16 at 2.1.11 on this platform, an EMPTY character-corpse is culled by the engine within ~400 ticks while a corpse holding seven iron plates survives, so an unstocked cell would be gone before any export scanned it

space-platform-hub.reason: the staging platform's own hub IS the space-platform-hub cell, and the surface census confirms exactly one hub stands on the platform, so the type is in any payload the fixture produces; the premise that a SECOND hub would be refused is NOT measured — creating one was never attempted, because a hub is what makes a platform a platform and a failed attempt could cost the staging surface
